repairAssignments.decisiveDefect: participant-instructions.md is a list of blanks and nothing else. It never names the court or the bureau the route files with, never states a waiver route for either fee, and never states who must be served or how; and it declares one blank a participant obligation that the source form reserves to the bureau.

failedProofObligations.finding: Of the 13 blanks the map declares REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, every one is named in participant-instructions.md except UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION p2 "SID#R&F" (blankId p2-y37.35-x188.34). No instruction line asks the participant to write a SID number or an R&F number. It is not merely unnamed: reading the source bytes at that position shows the blank sits inside the form's printed "BUREAU USE ONLY" box (heading read at page 2 y=51, x=26.93), and the family's own field census marks the same blank protectCategory "government_identifier". A blank the bureau completes cannot be an item the participant must supply before filing.

participant-instructions.md never tells the participant where to file. It lists "Judicial district and court street address for the filing venue" as a blank the participant must supply, which is the opposite of naming the destination, and it never mentions the Utah Bureau of Criminal Identification, which issues the certificate of eligibility the route names, or the district court that receives the petition. The packet's own caption does carry route-determined evidence of a destination — the "In the [ ] District [ ] Justice Court of Utah" election is marked District and the county is written — but a marked caption box is not the instructions naming a court.

The court filing fee is stated: the packet fills and selects the district-court cover sheet row "$150 [ ] Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)" on 1044XX page 2, proved by an X read from the output bytes at x355.98 y359.1 inside that row's bracket. No waiver route is stated anywhere in the packet or the instructions — no fee-waiver motion is included, named or referenced. The BCI certificate step carries its own fee, and the instructions name it only as a blank ('BCI payment or fee-waiver election and any payment details') without stating an amount or a waiver route.

The instructions never state who must be served or how. The only service line, "Service method, address, date, and certification only after service occurs", hands the participant the method and the recipient as blanks to fill in, and the closing sentence records that service certifications are protected. Neither names a recipient or a method.

repairAssignments.repairScope: Two separable repairs. (1) A packet-instruction repair lane rewrites participant-instructions.md to name the filing destinations the route names — the Utah Bureau of Criminal Identification for the certificate of eligibility and the district court for the petition — and to state the service recipient and method and the waiver route, from sourced facts only. The court filing fee is already stated on the cover sheet the packet fills and needs no invention; the BCI fee, both waiver routes and the service rule are not established in this repository and must reach the packet through a source lane, not through a verifier's or a builder's inference. (2) A field-map repair lane re-dispositions UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION blankId p2-y37.35-x188.34 from REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING to a protected agency-only disposition, matching the field census's own government_identifier category and the form's printed BUREAU USE ONLY region. Do not repair either in a verification lane.
repairAssignments.whatThisDoesNotChange: Eleven of the fifteen obligations pass on measurement made in this lane, including every source digest recomputed from the Master Library bytes and both artifact hashes recomputed from the PDF bytes. The packet's fill is sound; its participant-facing instructions and two blank dispositions are not.

repairAssignments.decisiveDefect: Two participant-facing statements that the packet's own bytes contradict, plus the CR-400 flattening defect FABLE-FIX06 root-caused on the sibling CR-409. participant-instructions.md tells the participant "The platform never marks a box on a sworn filing" while the delivered CR-400 content stream draws two diagonal X marks into two checkboxes in every one of the four fixtures; and production-field-map.json refuses fifteen controls on the recorded ground that "the participant instructions name it" while the instructions name none of the fifteen, including two waivers of rights and the five offence-section boxes that decide what the petition is about. Separately the delivered CR-400 footer caption is laid out on one line wider than the page: one word off the left edge and four unexplained same-baseline collisions, none present in the official baseline.

Proven from the inflated page content stream of fixtures/hs-11361-8-completed-sentence-application-canonical/cr-400-filled.pdf, not from the report: the operators "213.28 509.06 m ... 213.28 514.06 m" and "72.64 277.86 m ... 72.64 282.86 m" are the exact diagonal segments statutorySelectionProof records for CR-400[0].Page1[0].P1Caption[0].FormTitle[0].#area[1].Checkbox[1] (the § 11361.8(f) election) and CR-400[0].Page1[0].LI2[0].li2b[0].Checkbox[0] ("completed the sentence"). The currently-serving variant marks the mirror pair, § 11361.8(b) and "currently serving a sentence". Marking the statutory election may well be right; saying it is never done is not.

Fifteen refusals in production-field-map.json carry the reason "A control the participant marks. The platform never marks an election on a sworn filing; the participant instructions name it and the participant marks it before signing." participant-instructions.md names none of them: zero occurrences of 11357, 11358, 11359, 11360, 11362.1, "waives the right", "gives up that right", "sentencing judge", "Personal service", "Mail:" and "A.M.". Its blanks table lists only the 25 CR-401 proof-of-service fields and not one CR-400 control. Two of the fifteen are waivers: CR-400 LI3, waiving the right to have the matter heard by the original sentencing judge, and LI4, giving up the right to attend the hearing. Five more are the offence-section boxes. The refusal reason is the disclosure the packet claims to make and it does not make it.

The committed track registry gives ca-prop64 three selfHelpStopConditions. The string CR-402 appears nowhere in participant-instructions.md although the registry names it three times for this route — in selfHelpStopConditions, in destination.detail ("a prosecuting-agency response mechanism at CR-402") and in rules.notice ("The prosecuting agency responds at CR-402") — and the packet reduces a named form and mechanism to "if anyone opposes the petition". The word "hearing" does not appear at all, so "The court sets a contested hearing" is absent entirely; it is the one condition that does not require anyone to oppose anything. The registry's fourth boundary, "A routine hearing does not block the initial packet. A prosecuting-agency response at CR-402 or a contested hearing triggers handoff", is the distinction the packet loses. The same paragraph opens "This packet states what the repository holds for this route and nothing beyond it", which is untrue as to both.

repairAssignments.decisiveDefect: Two of the six self-help stop conditions the committed track registry records for nc_146_dismissal_petition are absent from the packet, with none of their distinguishing terms anywhere in participant-instructions.md. failedProofObligations.finding: Measured condition by condition against data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json trackId nc_146_dismissal_petition, selfHelpStopConditions, six entries. Four are carried, well: the G.S. 15A-1008 incapable-to-proceed dismissal with its statute, the DNA expunction under G.S. 15A-146(b1) with its 20-day service requirement, any immigration matter twice, and the deferred-prosecution or conditional-discharge dismissal in substance in the fee section. Two are absent. (1) "A felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement." participant-instructions.md contains zero occurrences of "plea agreement" and zero of "felony". (2) "Anyone who may later need G.S. 15A-145.4 or 15A-145.6 relief, because sequencing matters." Zero occurrences of 15A-145.4, of 15A-145.6, and of any form of the word sequence. failedProofObligations.finding: The A4 sentence quoted above is on the delivered guidance page of both fixtures. The timetable it denies is established for this exact route in data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json trackId pa_pardon_expungement three times over — packetInstructions: "Tell the participant a pardon does not by itself erase the record, and that the Board transmits eligible records to the AOPC quarterly"; manualCompletionItems: "Quarterly verification date — Guidance, verification schedule — The participant records when they checked whether the automatic route cleared the record", marked required before filing; and the petition component's own condition, "Generated only where the automatic route has not cleared the record after the quarterly cycle" — and a fourth time in src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/PA-pennsylvania.json: "the Board of Pardons transmits eligible records to AOPC quarterly, AOPC sends the record to the court of common pleas, and the court orders expungement after confirming the criteria." The packet's own participant-instructions.md paragraph 4 states the quarterly cycle in bold. So the page that goes in the envelope denies what the page that does not goes on to state. The guidance page compounds it by narrowing its source universe to "the two forms this packet is built from", which is the narrowing A2 forbids: the repository's committed records are held sources. In consequence the registry's named verification schedule appears nowhere on the guidance page. Structurally, the family also carries no "when to stop and get help" section on any page, and none of the registry's three selfHelpStopConditions is carried as a stop: the participant has not yet obtained a pardon and the pardon application is out of scope and a referral; whether the pardon is conditional or unconditional cannot be determined from the document; and the record still appears after the quarterly cycle with the fallback route's availability unclear.

The two that vanish are the petitioner's own state and ZIP. scripts/build-census-v1-pa_pardon_expungement-set.mjs holds them for the boundary persona at lines 271-272 — participant.state "Pennsylvania", participant.zip "18702-2214" — and maps both as WRITE at lines 108-109. The cause is a width refusal and both refusals are substantively correct: measured with pdf-lib Helvetica metrics against the widget rectangles in production-field-map.json, at the 6 pt readable floor "Pennsylvania" is 35.23 pt against an 18.21 pt AddrState widget and "18702-2214" is 32.02 pt against a 31.85 pt AddrZip widget, 0.17 pt too wide. Under docs/RCAP_OREGON_OFFICIAL_PDF_GRADE_A_LANE_C.md refusing at the floor is correct; the failure is the other half of that rule. Nothing records either refusal — reports/actual-writes.json has no refusal entry for the boundary petition, reports/builder-completeness-counters.json reports invisibleWrites 0 and findings empty — and neither field is among the field map's 78 requiredBeforeFiling entries or anywhere in participant-instructions.md.

All 78 declared required-before-filing blanks are disclosed and I checked every label myself: zero missing. The failure is what the list omits. AddrState and AddrZip become blanks the participant must fill the moment the finalizer refuses them, and they are not on the list, not on the page and not classified anywhere. The disclosure is complete against the builder's declaration and incomplete against the artifact it delivers.

What fails is the completeness of the artifact record: the boundary artifact carries two fewer writes than the canonical artifact of the same document and no record in the family explains the difference — no refusedWrites, no unfittable list, no note, invisibleWrites 0, findings empty. A reader of the record cannot tell that two values were refused.

repairAssignments.decisiveDefect: The packet never tells the participant where self-help ends. The committed track registry records eight selfHelpStopConditions for az_marijuana_expungement_limited_jurisdiction and the packet carries one paraphrased sentence covering three of them. Five are absent from the entire family directory, and two of those five are hard eligibility boundaries the registry ALSO records as exclusions: conduct on or after 12 July 2021, and a sale or any other non-listed marijuana offence. A petitioner outside either boundary is not eligible under A.R.S. § 36-2862 at all, and nothing in this packet tells them so before they file. The immigration condition, which every other family in this cohort carries, is also absent.

failedProofObligations.finding: Registry track az_marijuana_expungement_limited_jurisdiction records 8 selfHelpStopConditions (and 9 selfHelpBoundaries, and 3 exclusions). participant-instructions.md carries exactly one stop-adjacent sentence: 'Opposition, disputed evidence, or a contested hearing requires a post-generation handoff.' — a paraphrase of the single postGenerationHandoffs entry. It covers conditions 1-3. Conditions 4-8 appear nowhere. This was measured by searching the WHOLE family directory, not only the instructions: grep -ril over all 14 files for 'July 12', 'immigration', 'sale', 'appeal' and 'challenge the underlying' returns nothing, and no file in the family carries selfHelpStop, stopCondition or SELF_HELP in any form. The '2021' hits in the canonical PDF are the fixture case number M-2021-004217 and are unrelated. By contrast, all four composed-pleading families read in this same cohort carry a SELF_HELP_STOP entry in the field map's participantFacingObligations AND a 'When to stop and get help instead of filing' section enumerating every recorded condition (az_wrongful 4/4, in_infraction 4/4, ms 15/15 across three tracks, ny 5/5). The gap tracks the builder, not the state: this is the official_pdf_fill path, which emits neither structure.

omittedStopConditionsVerbatim: Conduct date is on or after July 12, 2021.
The offense is a sale or any other non-listed marijuana offense.
The petitioner wants to challenge the underlying conviction rather than expunge it.

Any marijuana offense outside the three statutory descriptions, including sale.
